question: Comparing the unilateral (1 tail) and bilateral hypothesis tests (2 tails):

options.opa: Bilateral tests always give higher p values.
options.opb: Bilateral tests always give lower p values.
options.opc: If a unilateral test is significant, so will the bilateral test.
options.opd: A bilateral test is more sensitive than a unilateral test.

analysis: In hypothesis testing, a bilateral (two-tailed) test considers both directions of an effect, while a unilateral (one-tailed) test considers only one direction. As a result, bilateral tests generally have higher p-values than unilateral tests for the same data, because the significance level is split between two tails. Therefore, if a unilateral test is significant, the bilateral test may not be, as the latter requires more extreme data to reach significance. A bilateral test is not more sensitive; it is more conservative because it requires evidence in both directions. Thus, option opa is correct.
